tasks.short: Record production, repair and machine-maintenance information

steps.what: Gather actual production, repair, parts-use and maintenance observations
Enter machine, work-order, parts, time and reading fields in the maintenance record
Write the actual fault, repair and maintenance outcome narrative
Check source consistency and complete the maintenance history entry

tasks.design: Configure existing asset/work-order context in the maintenance-management category {OTHER} to reuse identifiers and planned job fields in the original maintenance entry. Keep actual readings, quantities, time corrections, repair narrative and complete source checks with the worker; ordinary saving is retained without an approval gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job identity is repeatedly typed while actual findings still require technician capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mobile work-order forms can reuse existing context.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate fault descriptions and distinguishing planned parts from actual parts used.
tasks.human_edge: Record what happened rather than confirm a plausible planned outcome.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated context entry; unchanged maintenance-history responsibility.

evidence.claim: Ultimo provides preventive plans, repair history and mobile work orders; these support native maintenance context and record capability, not the proposed percentage.

assumptions: Boundary is the existing maintenance history used by planners and subsequent technicians. Shares are provisional and not measured.

Planning maintains asset identifier, work-order number and planned task; the worker produces actual readings, production status, start/stop times and parts quantities during the job, gathers/checks them in s1 and enters them in s2-s3. No free sensor feed, transcript or inferred parts use is assumed.

Test native work-order context first. Only repeated identifiers and planned task field entry, 20% of s2, is removed. Actual values, corrections, source checking and ordinary author save remain fully retained. Missing or wrong context is repaired in retained s2/s4.

This entry is documentation, not a machine release, work-order commercial close or equipment restart authorisation. Any actual formal release needs its own final-version approval and action; no same-system save gate is added.
unknowns: Current context already filled by the native form
Actual manual field entry and repairs
research_questions: Can native context remove repeated identifiers without presenting planned values as actual observations?

already_counted.description: Actual source capture, factual narrative and final consistency checks remain.

incremental.description: Worker checks field defaults after asset or work-order changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 35*0.20=7 repeated-context hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 6 net. Cautious case: an unplanned repair lacks most job context, leaving only 1.5 hours of known asset-field reuse and 0.5 net; actual readings and narrative remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate to repair or move machinery and parts

steps.what: Read the existing job brief and machinery handling requirements
Agree repair or movement roles and safe coordination with other workers
Collaborate physically in repairing or moving machinery, parts or equipment

tasks.design: Retain coordination and physical collaboration, using the existing {DOCS} brief and maintenance-management category {OTHER} work order. Native access already provides the brief; no additional system change removes the actual work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe machinery movement and repair require coordinated people and physical handling.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change replaces that coordination or handling.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected loads, access constraints and maintaining clear communication.
tasks.human_edge: React to coworkers and actual machinery conditions together.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: machinery handling and collaborative repair require physical coordination and safety judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is this worker's collaboration, not coworkers' separately counted labour. Provisional shares are not measured.
Planning supplies the existing brief and handling requirements, checked in s1. Coworkers and the worker agree the approach in s2; no new structured movement plan or transcript is assumed.

Any actual maintenance entry from this work is owned once by task 11834. If a separate permit or lifting plan must be written here, split its actual first write and any authorised release before estimating benefit. Do not invent a collaboration log.
Native brief access is already present. No removed lookup or new system is established, so upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Does this collaboration require an actual separate written permit or handling plan?

already_counted.description: Brief reading, coordination and physical work remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains. A constrained machinery movement still requires full coordination and handling; no coworker labour or invented movement log is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read orders and specifications to identify maintenance requirements

steps.what: Find the current work order and matching machine specification revision
Read work orders and specifications for required repairs or maintenance
Determine affected machines and clarify ambiguous scope before work

tasks.design: Configure native asset-document links from the maintenance-management category {OTHER} to the current specification in {DOCS}. Remove repeated folder and revision-index navigation while retaining document applicability checks, technical reading and scope clarification.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct specification can be separated from the assigned work order.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset-linked document references can expose the original revision.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting unclear repair scope and noticing a mismatch with the actual machine.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge the job brief before unsafe or unnecessary work.
tasks.altitude: Less navigation, with unchanged technical interpretation.

evidence.claim: Ultimo supports preventive plans, mobile work orders and repair history; native asset-linked source access is plausible configuration, with local availability to verify.

assumptions: Boundary ends at understood and clarified work scope, not physical maintenance or a new work report. Shares are provisional.

Planning provides order identifier and asset identifier; engineering maintains the specification document link, revision and applicability. The worker checks actual asset match in s1/s3. Missing or stale links require manual document search within retained s1 and clarification s3.
Test native asset-document links first. Only folder/revision-index navigation, 25% of s1, is removed; applicability checks and all technical reading stay.

No new structured document extraction or unpriced link catalogue is assumed. If engineering must create missing links, count that extra labour before rollout. No trailing scope-confirmation log is invented.
research_questions: Do native links reach the correct current specification without new manual catalogue building?

already_counted.description: Applicability checks, failed-link fallback and scope clarification remain.

incremental.description: Worker checks document-link validity after asset changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25*0.25=6.25 navigation hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 5.75 net. Cautious case: a modified legacy machine needs manual revision research, leaving 0.8 hours of known-link navigation removed and 0.3 net; technical reading remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect damaged parts, mark defects and advise supervisors

steps.what: Check part specifications and permitted inspection or test procedure
Inspect or test damaged machine parts against the criteria
outputs: observed part defects and test results

steps.what: Mark identified defective areas on the machine part
inputs: observed part defects and test results

steps.what: Write actual defect findings and repair needs in the supervisor report
inputs: observed part defects and test results

steps.what: Check final defect report, part identity and supervisor destination
inputs: observed part defects and test results
outputs: final checked defect report and supervisor

steps.what: Send the checked repair-needs report to the supervisor
inputs: final checked defect report and supervisor

tasks.design: Use native asset and part context in the maintenance-management category {OTHER} defect-report form. Retain inspection, testing, physical marking and actual finding entry; check the completed report before its separate supervisor send.
tasks.previous_blocker: The report must distinguish an observed defect from a proposed repair.
tasks.enabler_now: Native context can remove repeated asset/part identity fields.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing damage and knowing when specialist testing is required.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe defects and communicate uncertainty accurately.
tasks.altitude: Less report identity entry; unchanged inspection judgement.

evidence.claim: Ultimo supports mobile work orders and repair history; using native asset context for fault reporting is supported by its maintenance-record capability.

assumptions: Boundary is the branch with both physical defect marking and an actual supervisor repair-needs report. Mark-only or spoken-only advice branches require their own observed mix; shares are provisional.

The worker produces actual results in s2 and marks defects in s3, then captures findings in s4. Planning maintains asset/part identifiers. No free sensor reading, image diagnosis or structured defect description is assumed.

Test native context first. Only repeated asset/part identifiers, 10% of s4, are removed; observed measurements, explanation, repairs and ordinary draft saving remain fully retained. s5 retains wrong-context correction and meaning checks.

s5 checks the final complete report and exact supervisor before s6; edits void approval. The report is a real handoff, not an author save. Maintenance history task 11834 should reuse this same finding rather than charge duplicate narrative entry in a roll-up.
unknowns: Actual written versus spoken supervisor advice
Duplicate narrative ownership with maintenance history
research_questions: Can one actual finding record serve the supervisor and maintenance history without duplicate entry?

already_counted.description: Finding capture, context repairs and final report checks remain.

incremental.description: Worker checks fault form context after asset changes.

approvals.approved_version: s5 final defect report, exact part and supervisor destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.10=2 identity-entry hours removed less 0.4 upkeep gives 1.6 net. Cautious case: an unregistered replacement part needs manual identification, leaving 0.5 hours of machine-context reuse and 0.1 net; inspection and marking remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native maintenance context and source links reduce repeated entry and navigation, while physical repair, inspection and collaboration stay with the worker.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish actual from planned maintenance values
role.ambitious_version: No automatic machinery release or replacement of physical maintenance is proposed.
